name: pay-first-won
about: One concept clearly did well over many leads and one spent for nothing.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Our ads with hook pay_first (pay first) and scene equipment_on_road (truck on the road) spent $612.40 in the last 28 days over 48210 impressions and brought 31 leads, $19.75 per lead.
Our ads with hook life_first (life first) and scene home_street (home street) spent $188.00 in the last 28 days over 15120 impressions and brought no lead.
Of 31 of our ad leads in the last 28 days, 29 were called and 22 were reached.

output.audience: Class A drivers who meet the experience requirement and want flatbed work on Midwest regional lanes. They are likely driving now and comparing offers. The pay per mile, home weekly and an assigned truck at a small fleet are what would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile over a loaded flatbed running a Midwest highway.
angles.proof: The opening states the pay per mile for flatbed work on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: This pairing brought all the earlier leads at a cost per lead well under the benchmark pause line, and recruiters reached most of them. It is the base to build on.

angles.idea: Say plainly from the driver's seat who the job is for: Class A, the experience requirement, Midwest regional lanes.
angles.proof: The opening is a Class A regional job that states an experience requirement and runs Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Untested pairing. The lead outcomes show who was reached, not who qualified, so an ad that states the requirement and the area plainly helps recruiter calls count.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck, shown parked and ready with a flatbed trailer behind it.
angles.proof: The opening lists an assigned truck and flatbed freight.
angles.why: Nothing has been measured for this pairing. The assigned truck is a concrete fact the pay ads do not carry, and it speaks to drivers who care what they drive.

angles.idea: Open on the small fleet where dispatch knows your name, then list home weekly and the retirement plan as plain text.
angles.proof: The carrier describes itself this way, and the opening lists home weekly and the retirement plan.
angles.why: Nothing measured for this pairing. Home weekly is carried here as a stated term because the home street ads spent and brought no lead.
